findings.measured: The audio is still loud at the last sample; the ending may be cut off.

steps.text: In the Bounce window, turn on Include Audio Tail (or extend the cycle range past the last tail).

other_options.text: Set a Fade Out on the last region in the Region inspector, then bounce again.

notes.headline: This master measures clean across the board; the only real issue is that the file stops while audio is still playing, so re-bounce with the tail included.
notes.summary: Technically this is release-ready at 9.4/10 — integrated loudness sits at -14.38 LUFS with true peak at -1.27 dBTP, so nothing is clipping and you have plenty of headroom against streaming targets. Stereo behavior is healthy too: correlation of 0.785, low end at 0.793, and only 0.5 dB lost in mono. The one thing to fix is the ending: the audio is still loud at the last sample, which means the tail is being chopped off in the bounce.

priorities.title: Cut-off ending
priorities.why: The file ends mid-sound, so listeners and streaming players will hear an abrupt click or truncation instead of the song finishing. It's a bounce setting, not a mix problem.

listen_for: Play the last few seconds of the re-bounced file all the way to silence — no click or sudden stop at the final sample.
Check the tail on headphones and on a phone speaker; short truncations are easiest to miss on small speakers.
Confirm the reverb or final note decays fully rather than being clipped by the cycle range.
strengths: True peak of -1.27 dBTP leaves safe headroom for lossy encoding.
Integrated loudness of -14.38 LUFS with 13.1 dB peak-to-loudness keeps the dynamics intact for release.
Stereo image is solid: 0.785 correlation, 0.793 in the low end, only 0.5 dB mono loss, and left/right balance within 0.02 dB.
